blocks.text: Private Cloud Controllers behave as a per-tenant controller for users, Private Service Edges for Private Access (ZPA), and App Connectors to leverage when the Private Access cloud is not available or reachable.
Private Cloud Controllers provide the following benefits, and perform the following functionalities:

blocks.item: Downloads and persists a complete copy of customer configuration and policies.
Distributes customer configuration and policies to onsite Private Service Edges and App Connectors when Business Continuity is enabled.
Acts as an authentication redirection endpoint when Business Continuity is enabled.
Allows for log streaming to a SIEM when Business Continuity is enabled.
Redirects users to Private Service Edges when Business Continuity is enabled.

blocks.text: To provide application access during a global Private Access outage, you must configure, enroll, and maintain Private Cloud Controllers. In addition, to ensure that Business Continuity functions properly, Private Cloud Controllers must run on the same or a later software version as the App Connectors and Private Service Edges. To learn more, see Configuring Private Cloud Controllers.
Private Cloud Controller certificate enrollment is valid for one year. To automatically refresh the certificate enrollment, configure the Certificate Renewal Threshold when adding a Private Cloud.

blocks.heading: About the Private Cloud Controllers Page

blocks.text: On the Private Cloud Controllers page (Infrastructure > Business Continuity > Private Cloud Controllers), you can do the following:

blocks.item: View a list of applied filters available from the current and previous user sessions. Applied filters must be saved to the user session first before they can be viewed. Use the drop-down menu to select the applied filters to view. To learn more, see Using Tables.
Hide the filters on the page by clicking Hide Filters. Click Show Filters to display the filters.
Refresh the Private Cloud Controller Controllers page to reflect the most current information.
Filter the information that appears in the table. You can also save applied filters to your preferences so that they're visible in future user sessions. To learn more, see Using Tables.
Add a Private Cloud Controller.
Private Cloud Controllers that are managed by Zscaler are read only and cannot be configured. To learn more, see Understanding Zscaler-Managed Business Continuity Cloud.
View a list of deployed Private Cloud Controllers. Private Cloud Controllers that you've added, but have not deployed, are not listed.
Name: The name of the Private Cloud Controller. OAuth-enabled Private Cloud Controllers are added with a name format of GroupName-UserCode-TimeStamp.
View details for each deployed Private Cloud Controller.
Description: The description of the Private Cloud Controller, if available.
Private Cloud Controller Group: The Private Cloud Controller group that the Private Cloud Controller is a member of.
Enrollment Certificate: The certificate of the Private Cloud Controller used for enrollment. You can click the Edit icon to edit the properties of the certificate.
Host Platform: The platform that the Private Cloud Controller is deployed on (e.g., AWS).
Host OS: The run time OS on which the Private Cloud Controller is running (e.g., RHEL Linux 9).
Package OS: The compile time OS on which the RPM binary is packaged (e.g., Enterprise Linux 9).
Last Software Update: The date and time the Private Cloud Controller was last updated to a later software version.
Last Manager Update: The date and time the Manager software was last updated to a later software version.
Last OS Update: The date and time the OS was last updated to a later software version.
Public Service Edge: The Public Service Edge that the Private Cloud Controller connects to.
Last Connection to Zscaler: The last time the Private Cloud Controller connected to Zscaler.
Last Disconnect from Zscaler: The last time the Private Cloud Controller disconnected from Zscaler.
Location: The location where the Private Cloud Controller group that the Private Cloud Controller belongs to is set up.
Public IP: The public IP address of the Private Cloud Controller. Disconnected Private Cloud Controllers show the last known public IP address.
Private IP: The private IP address of the Private Cloud Controller. Disconnected Private Cloud Controllers show the last known private IP address.
Uptime: The period of time the Private Cloud Controller is available for use. Disconnected Private Cloud Controllers show the value Not Available.
Enrollment Time: The date and time the Private Cloud Controller was enrolled.
Business Continuity SP FQDN: The Business Continuity Service Provider FQDN.
Supporting Files Upgrade Status: The upgrade status and the current version of the supporting files mapping the Private Cloud Controller public IP address to its registered country.
Operating System Updates: Indicates whether automatic updates for the OS are enabled or disabled.

Automated OS security updates are only available for Private Cloud Controller images on RHEL 9.x. Private Cloud Controllers installed manually using an RPM file on a custom RHEL 9.x build are not supported.
Connection Health: The health of the Private Cloud Controller connection (Connected or Disconnected).
Secure Shell (SSH): Indicates whether the default OS SSH setting is overridden and enabled or disabled.
Manager Version: The version of the current Private Cloud Controller Manager software. To learn more, see Understanding the Manager Software.
Software Version: The current Private Cloud Controller software version.

Version Profile: The version profile applied to the Private Cloud Controller. You can hover over the Information icon to view a description of the Default, Previous Default, or New Release for the version profile. If a Custom version profile is configured, you can hover over the Custom link to view details for it.
Connection Status: The status of the Private Cloud Controller connection.
Software Update: The status of the last Private Cloud Controller software update.
Status: Indicates whether the Private Cloud Controller is enabled or disabled.

Manager Update: The status of the Private Cloud Controller update. You can hover over the Information icon next to the update status to view more information, such as the scheduled version and upgrade window.

OS Update: The status of the OS update (Scheduled, Not Scheduled, In Progress, Success, or Failure). You can hover over the Information icon to view more information, such as the update window and status of the update.
Modify the columns displayed in the table.
Edit the configuration of a deployed Private Cloud Controller.
Delete a deployed Private Cloud Controller.
Private Cloud Controllers that are managed by Zscaler are read only and cannot be edited or deleted. To learn more, see Understanding Zscaler-Managed Business Continuity Cloud.
